text:
maria.g: FYI customer 'Lexico' reporting intermittent high tail latency on the embeddings endpoint this morning. 99th ~2.1s vs usual ~120ms. No 4xx/5xx in their traces, just long service time. Happening since ~09:10 UTC.
ajay.s: thanks, can you paste a sample request and any request_ids? also did they change SDK version or model variant?
maria.g: sample request id: req_2026_00041. They use embed-small-v2, SDK 1.4.2. No recent code changes on their side per account engineer. Attaching quick curl we reproduced: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-small-v2","input":["apple","banana","car"],"client_meta":{"tag":"lexico-prod"}}'
```
sam.k: I pulled the route logs for req_2026_00041. I see a series of batches where one worker holds a batch open waiting for drain, then the next flush contains a big padding jump. snippet: 
```
[09:10:11.003] batch_open id=42 size=2 target=8 wait_ms=120
[09:10:11.125] batch_add  id=42 size=3
[09:10:11.127] batch_flush id=42 size=3 padded_to=256 processing_ms=1750
```
ajay.s: padded_to=256?? that sounds wrong for embed-small-v2 (expected 64). Any chance a malformed request with extra dims slipped in?
maria.g: customer payloads look normal. But they did flip on a per-request "client_meta.max_sequence" annotation last week for a different feature. could that be leaking into batch sizing?
sam.k: possible. Dynamic batching uses an inferred size key that should be model_dim + client hints. If a client_meta field accidentally contains a very large numeric, it could be treated as sequence length and cause padding.
infra-bot: noticed periodic auth token refresh on the region at 09:10 with ~0.5% increased latency to KMS; some workers saw longer auth handshake and temporarily queued requests.
ajay.s: that fits a scenario: auth delay holds open leader batch, later many small queued requests get coalesced and padded to the largest hinted size present in the batch. leads to huge processing time for a few batches -> tail spikes.
maria.g: can we repro locally? steps I did: 1) run local dynbatch worker, 2) send mix of normal small embeds and a single request with client_meta.max_sequence=1024 3) add artificial delay to auth call. result: same tail spike and padded_to jumped to 1024.
ajay.s: please capture the worker debug trace and the batch key calculation. Add environment var REDWOOD_DYNBATCH_DEBUG=1 then send: 
```
# repro script (bash)
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  if [ $i -eq 7 ]; then
    curl -s -X POST $URL -d '{"model":"embed-small-v2","input":["big"],"client_meta":{"max_sequence":1024}}' &
  else
    curl -s -X POST $URL -d '{"model":"embed-small-v2","input":["a"]}' &
  fi
done
```
support-ops: noted, we've been seeing a handful of tenant SDKs pass free-form client_meta keys. We should tighten the dynamic batching key extraction to only accept trusted fields (e.g., sequence_length) and ignore numeric-looking client_meta keys.
sam.k: short-term mitigation: set per-route max_padding_limit=128 for embed-small-v2 so any inferred pad above that is clipped. Also deploy a fast check that drops unexpected client_meta numeric hints.
ajay.s: opened internal ticket #INF-7421 for batching key hardening + rollout config. action items for oncall: 1) apply max_padding_limit=128 to prod for embed-small-v2 2) add a metric: batch_padded_above_limit{route="embed-small-v2"} 3) follow up with Lexico with repro steps and ask them to remove free-form numeric client_meta.
maria.g: I'll contact the customer and run the repro script with them. thanks all :thumbsup:
